data.title: Micron or CoreWeave: One Stock Is a Strong Buy After Today's Drop, but the Other Has More Upside, According to Wall Street
data.description:
Tech stocks are taking a beating on Friday, with the Nasdaq sinking about 2.2% as investors reconsider their enthusiasm for AI. Concerns about expensive data centers, stretched valuations, and the sustainability of massive technology spending are weighing heavily on companies closely associated with the AI boom.

Among the most talked-about names are Micron (NASDAQ:MU) and CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV), two companies that have benefited tremendously from the AI boom. Micron, a leading supplier of advanced memory chips, is losing about 5.5% on Friday, while neocloud specialist CoreWeave is plunging 12% amid mounting concerns about its debt and financing costs.

According to Wall Street, while Micron earns a Strong Buy consensus rating, CoreWeave comes with greater risks but also offers much higher potential returns. After all, greater risk often comes with the possibility of greater rewards.

Micron's Record Earnings Can't Keep Investors Happy

Micron has become one of the biggest beneficiaries of soaring demand for high-bandwidth memory, an essential component of advanced AI processors. Companies such as Nvidia rely on these specialized chips to support sophisticated computing systems, creating an attractive opportunity for memory manufacturers.

The company's latest financial results demonstrated just how profitable this opportunity has become. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue reached $54.23 billion, representing a staggering 379% increase from the previous year, while adjusted earnings reached $33.42 per share. Looking ahead, Micron expects fiscal first-quarter revenue between $60 billion and $63 billion, suggesting customer demand remains strong.

However, investors have found a new reason to worry following recent developments in China. Chinese memory manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies announced progress on a more compact DRAM chip design that could increase storage density, alongside plans to introduce a new server-memory product before year-end. The announcement has raised concerns that Chinese competitors could eventually challenge established manufacturers and weaken the favorable pricing conditions supporting their profits.

Still, analysts caution that CXMT's technological progress doesn't necessarily represent an immediate threat to Micron. The Chinese manufacturer's ability to produce these advanced chips commercially remains uncertain, while its latest developments do not directly challenge the high-bandwidth memory products used in leading AI systems.

Nevertheless, the news has added to broader concerns about future memory supply and the sustainability of today's elevated profit margins. Following Micron's tremendous rally over the past year, investors appear less willing to overlook potential risks, particularly as semiconductor stocks continue struggling.

Wall Street, however, remains bullish on Micron's prospects, despite the recent selloff. MU stock earns a Strong Buy consensus rating, with 27 Buys and just one Hold among 28 recent analyst recommendations. Meanwhile, the average 12-month price target stands at $1,621.67, suggesting upside potential of ~85% from current levels. (See MU stock forecast)
data.author: Ben Yoffe

data.title: CoreWeave Stock (CRWV) Plunges Another 12% as the AI Trade Unwinds
data.description:
The stock of CoreWeave (CRWV) is down another 12% on Oct. 16 as the trade in stocks tied to the artificial intelligence (AI) trade unwinds and investors rotate capital into blue-chip names. For the week, CRWV stock is down 25% as investors grow increasingly concerned with the amount of debt that companies such as CoreWeave are taking on to fund the AI buildout.

In late afternoon trading on Oct. 16, the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite index is down more than 600 points, or 2.25%, as investors move money into other areas of the stock market. In addition to CoreWeave, stocks such as Nebius Group (NBIS) and Strategy (MSTR) were down more than 10%. At the same time, blue-chip names such as Coca-Cola (KO) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) were rising.

data.title: Tesla Cars May Fly But TSLA Stock Doesn't
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) stock retreated 3.26% on Friday, despite an over 2% rally earlier in the day. The catalyst for that rally was the Tesla Roadster event last night. Founder and CEO Elon Musk showed off the new Tesla Roadster EV, with the highlight being the vehicle's ability to fly for a short period of time.

The Tesla Roadster reveal started with the EV making its way up a half-loop ramp and launching off of it upside down. While midair, compressors fired and adjusted the car to be upright, before slowing its descent, allowing it to safely land on the ground. The presentation continued with other fun tricks, including having the Roadster do a spinning jump over several of Tesla's other vehicles, including its semi truck.

Why Did Tesla Stock Fail to Fly Today?

While the Tesla Roadster showcase was flashy and an impressive feat of engineering, it was more show than substance. The Roadster equipped for those fancy aerial moves is only available to invited customers. That squashed any hopes that the future of flying cars was just around the corner. This version of the EV also only features a single seat due to the other equipment in it, which hampers the appeal of the EV.

Promotion

High conviction on SPCX? Try Tradr's SPCM or SPCG

Even so, there are two other versions of the Tesla Roadster available for preorder. There's a base version that comes without any of the fancy compressors, as well as a limited model that features compressors for boosting. Tesla showed that this allows the limited model of the EV to go from zero to 60 mph in just one second. While that's fun, it did raise some concerns about usability and the effect that compressing more air will have on the EV's battery.

Adding to Tesla's problems was a weak stock market. The overall market took a strong beating, as tech stocks experienced a selloff. That especially affected those in the AI sector, which included TSLA shares.

This sent TSLA stock 3.26% lower today, extending a 7.88% drop over the past five days. Sister company SpaceX (SPCX), which helped out with the design of the new Roadster, was down 3.62% as of this writing.

Is Tesla Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Tesla is Moderate Buy, based on 14 Buy, 11 Hold, and two Sell ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average TSLA stock price target of $404.87, representing a potential 15.68% upside for the shares. (See TSLA Stock Forecast)

data.title: Meta Still Needs to Show It Can Monetize Its Muse Agent, Says 5-Star BNP Analyst
data.description: Social media giant Meta Platforms (META) has surpassed 10.4 million downloads of its Muse AI assistant since its September launch, according to BNP Paribas (BNPQY). The investment bank said on Friday that the app's popularity remains strong after it overtook OpenAI's ChatGPT on Apple's (AAPL) U.S. App Store. However, five-star analyst Nick Jones, who has a 28.8% average return rate, believes Meta still needs to demonstrate that those downloads can translate into meaningful revenue, although he maintained a Buy rating and an $885 price target on the stock.

data.title: Why Are Gold and Silver Down Today, 10/16/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are trading lower on Friday with losses of 0.3% and 0.72%, respectively. Rising Treasury yields are pressuring the two precious metals, with the 10-year yield up 1.5 basis points (bps) to 5.1% and the 30-year yield up 1.1 bps to 5.43%.

With higher yields, the opportunity cost of holding gold and silver increases. That's because they don't pay out interest, making interest-bearing assets, like Treasuries, more attractive.

Yield, Dollar Strength Offsets Relief From Falling Rate Hike Bets

An elevated dollar is also weighing on the precious metals. While the U.S. Dollar Index is down 0.17% to 101.88 today, the index is still up by 3.52% year-to-date. A stronger dollar makes gold and silver more expensive for foreign buyers because they are priced in dollars.

data.title: Fractyl Health Stock (GUTS) Sinks Over 58% on Trial Results and a Lawsuit
data.description:
Fractyl Health (GUTS) stock took an over 58% beating on Friday, even after the company announced positive results from its REMAIN-1 study. The clinical-stage metabolic therapeutics company said the study met its pre-specified six-month co-primary endpoint of weight-loss retention.

According to Fractyl Health, patients who were treated with a single Revita DMR System procedure saw a strong increase in weight retention when compared with the sham group. The company highlighted that 32% of patients maintained weight or saw further weight loss six months after stopping use of a GLP-1 treatment. For comparison, this was only 18% for the sham group's results.

"We believe these 6-month results reinforce the potential of Revita to be the first durable procedural therapy for post-GLP-1 weight maintenance and support the Company's planned De Novo marketing application submission in late Q4 2026," the company said in a press release.

What This Means for GUTS Stock

GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are a hot topic right now, as patients seek ways to lose weight to avoid cardiac events or type 2 diabetes. However, keeping the weight off after their prescriptions end can be a problem. If Fractyl Health's Revita DMR System gets approval, it could offer a way for those patients to maintain or lose further weight after they quit taking a GLP-1 drug.

So Why Is GUTS Stock Down Today?

Fractyl Health stock was named in a class-action lawsuit filed today by Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC. This lawsuit is seeking damages from defendants over alleged violations of the federal securities laws. It claims that Fractyl Health "made false and/or misleading statements" in relation to its Revita DMR System study. The allegations include the weight-managmeent treatment being less effective than Fractyl Health previously stated, clinical, regulatory, and commercial prospects being overstated, and false public statements based on the previous claims.

Is Fractyl Health Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Fractyl Health is Strong Buy, based on four Buy and one Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average GUTS stock price target of $40, representing a potential 2,266.86% upside for the shares (See GUTS Stock Forecast)

data.title: Microsoft's (MSFT) Free Cash Flow Expected to Remain Positive Despite Heavy AI Spending
data.description:
Microsoft's (MSFT) free cash flow is expected to remain in positive territory despite the company's heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and infrastructure. In a new report, Bank of America (BAC) singles out Microsoft, saying the Seattle-based company stands alone among major technology companies as one of only a few that isn't expected to post negative free cash flow over the next year.

Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), Oracle (ORCL), and Meta Platforms (META) are each expected to fall into negative free cash flow in 2027, with Bank of America forecasting these so called "hyperscalers" next-twelve-month free cash flow estimates will drop significantly between by 2028 as spending on Ai accelerates.

Microsoft's AI Spending

Microsoft is spending heavily on AI. The company behind the Copilot digital assistant is expected to spend $175 billion to $190 billion in total capital expenditures this year, with the vast majority of that money going towards AI infrastructure such as data centers and microchips. The company is expected to spend even more in 2027.

Promotion

Technology investors who refuse to pick growth or income now have TDAQ.

The company has said that its capital expenditures could reach as much as Microsoft $260 billion in 2027, again with the majority of the money being funneled into AI projects and technologies. Yet despite the heavy spending, Microsoft is expected to continue generating positive free cash flow, distinguishing it from its mega-cap technology peers, says Bank of America.

The outlook isn't entirely bleak for the sector, according to BofA Global Research, which expects hyperscalers' free cash flow to shift from negative to positive by the second half of 2027 as AI-related revenue growth accelerates and AI capital expenditures decelerate.

However, the research firm warns of significant risk: AI capex has surprised to the upside by a much wider margin than revenue—50% versus 20% this year—meaning 2027 expectations imply a marked shift in trend.

BofA Global Research's estimated compute demand through 2030 implies approximately $10T of spend, roughly $2T above current forecasts.
